newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps inch up, CFDs up 3 ct, mogas well b.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps inch up, CFDs up 3 ct, mogas well b.

text.p: European oil swaps were slightly firmer on Wednesday morning but activity was thin, due partly to a public holiday in Holland.
Brent CFDs edged three cents higher for next week after physical cargoes traded at 27 cents under June compared to 29 under on Tuesday.
Next week's CFDs talked 28 cents under June and traded flat with the following week of 12-16 May.
Monthly CFDs remain in contango with May and June valued around 30 cents under the front line IPE Brent and 23 cents under respectively.
The third and fourth quarters were 14 cents and 12 cents under respectively with the whole of 1998 talking either side of five cents under the screen.
Gasoline talked around $198.50 for May about $2 above the $196 that talked for much of Tuesday.
"There was a late rally yesterday but the bids are still strong," said a broker.
He pegged gasoline crack spreads little changed at $5.25 a barrel for May, $4.05 for the third quarter and $3.10 for the fourth quarter.
Heavy fuel was little changed but narrow spreads between low and high sulphur continued to dominate trading.

May barges were valued around $81.50 a tonne with low sulphur just $3 higher. The market remains in a gentle contango until February next year with downward pressure on May due to poor demand throughout Europe.
Some dealers expected prices to stay under pressure due to recent high refinery runs which they say have boosted fuel production in recent weeks.
Middle distillates were little changed. Gas oil crack spreads against Brent talked $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97), $4.75 (1Q98), $4.10 (2Q98).
Swaps for physical gas oil cargoes held at $6 a tonne and $14.75 over the IPE for May 0.2 and EN590 respectively.
Jet premiums above the IPE also held steady. May was pegged around $24.50 a tonne over while June was $25.00 over.
